audience: the repository owner who reads and rates proposals
approved collaborators and agents filing observations on any repository in the stack
external contributors who need one understandable way to report what they saw
problem: The same issue-governance rule is hand-copied into several repositories, and the same version pins are written into many files. Copies drift, so a report filed in one repository does not match the trail in another and nobody can tell which copy is authoritative.
solution: One repository holds the observational-issue protocol — a three-plane, non-binding proposal form and the triage that labels it — so every other repository consumes one source instead of maintaining its own copy. Each adopter pins the protocol and the rest of the stack in one place.

evidence.claim: The observational-issue form is a three-plane, non-binding proposal with required provenance, reproducibility, citations, and a priority rating.
evidence.source: The issue template committed to this repository.
evidence.supports: The committed template file defines the exact fields a filed observation must carry.
evidence.limits: The template defines the form only; it does not prove that any adopter has switched to consuming it.

evidence.claim: An accepted plan of record covers the duplication, the loose files, a target folder tree for each repository, and a phased adoption order.
evidence.source: The cross-repository plan of record filed on the continuity repository.
evidence.supports: The plan issue records the audit, the duplication map, the loose-file inventory, the target trees, and the owner decisions that gate adoption.
evidence.limits: It is a non-binding proposal; no repository has been migrated to the shared source yet.

boundaries: Every observation filed under this protocol is a non-binding proposal, not a literal implementation mandate.
This repository owns the protocol and its triage; it does not own any adopter's product code or issues.
Adopters keep their own issue history; switching them to consume the shared source is a separate, owner-gated step.
